purpose: Test whether a source-family four-state HMM can signal out-of-distribution event timing/noise during a continuous unlabelled stream, versus simple raw switching
generator: Concatenate two independent event_segmentation episode observed arrays; no boundary fields passed to detector, boundary used only for scoring
methods: HMM predictive-surprise CUSUM calibrated on stationary training maxima
sliding-window HMM predictive-surprise mean calibrated on identical stationary training
raw adjacent-symbol change-rate monitor calibrated on identical stationary training

fixed_settings.score_rule: one-sided accumulated centered log surprise, baseline reference from source train only
fixed_settings.threshold: smallest observed calibration maximum with fewer than or equal to 10 percent strictly-greater maxima; ties not alarms

metrics: false-alarm episode count in 240 stationary test trials
detected changes out of 240 shifted test trials
mean negative predictive log likelihood by scenario
boundaries: Only tokens enter monitor; no simulator hidden labels, phase, boundary, or test rewards used by detector
No retuning after reading evaluation results
Six seeds inspected previously; not independent blind
No claims of safety from empirical false alarms
Preserve original benchmark and V2A/V2B order
